(1) Past two lines: of 2,476 US adults with incident SLE who started treatment, 418 (16.882%) reached a third sequence of therapy, a new sequence being a different SLE drug added or switched to more than 30 days after the last, over a mean 47.8 months' follow-up (Masurkar PP et al., Lupus Sci Med 2024;11(2), doi 10.1136/lupus-2024-001290, PMC11683911; MarketScan commercial and Medicare supplemental, first diagnosis 2013 to 2017). AUTOGRAPH requires an inadequate response to at least two therapies. (2) On treatment: 5,360 of 5,984 US adults with SLE (89.572%) filled an SLE medication in 2023 (Figueroa-Parra G et al., Lupus Sci Med 2024;11(2), PMC11629018; OptumLabs). 0.16882 x 0.89572 = 0.151216, about 30,890 US patients and 2,157 newly eligible a year

Pushing lower: a change of sequence can follow intolerance or non-persistence rather than an inadequate response, and the trial's SLEDAI-2K of 6 or more, age 18 to 75 and organ function criteria are not taken off. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 30.05% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 37.20%, so the charge rebuilds at -7.15%. It was held at nil, but NVS books $3,197mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001114448-26-000004), 5.86% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -5.86%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 NVS's cash flow statement shows receivables up $3,559mm, inventories up $737mm, payables up $101mm, a working capital build of $4,195mm, 2.79% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -5.86% where the filed figures rebuild it at -7.15%, and stays there.
